transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, my wife is the one who made the appointment. She got pretty scared recently. I keep... I keep hearing water running inside the walls. And men whispering in there, too, even when I know nobody else is around. And sometimes I'll look down the hallway and see this dark, wet patch spreading across the floor. But when I go over and check it, it's completely dry. I guess that's what finally made her insist I come see you.
When did you first start hearing the water running and the voices whispering in the walls?

It's been going on for about seven months. It started right around the winter freeze. The house repairs just... they turned into this massive mess that I couldn't get out from under. That's when I first started hearing it all.
Have you had any major illnesses, fevers, infections, head injuries, or been in an accident around the time the water sounds and voices started seven months ago?
No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick or hurt. No head injuries, no fevers, no accidents... just the stress of the house, really. Physically, I've been fine.
When you hear the voices and see that wet patch on the floor, do you believe these things are actually happening, or do you recognize that they might not be real?

Well, my wife keeps telling me it's not real, but... to me, it is. I mean, I know it sounds far-fetched, but I’m absolutely certain the mold and the bad wiring in that house have poisoned everything I own. It's in everything. And... I can tell the neighbors are watching us, too. They're just waiting to see when I mess up again. So, yes, I do believe it's actually happening.
Over these past seven months, have you been able to keep up with your job, your personal hygiene, and your daily responsibilities, or have these things fallen apart?

Well, things have definitely fallen apart. I've stopped keeping up with the basic repairs around the house, and I haven't been paying the bills or keeping up with any of my usual commitments. My wife has had to take over all the decisions that I used to handle myself. It actually got so bad recently that she had to call a crisis team... I just couldn't cooperate with a safety inspection they were trying to do at the house. I just couldn't do it.

Over these past seven months, have you had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or felt like your mood was elevated or unusually good—even if other things were falling apart?

No. No, definitely not. I haven't had any energy at all. I've just been feeling... heavy, and tired all the time. I haven't felt good or happy once in these past seven months. It's just been a constant struggle.

When you think about the mold, the wiring, the neighbors watching, and the voices in the walls—do these things feel connected to each other, like they're all part of one larger plot or conspiracy? Or do they feel like separate, unrelated things happening to you?

Like I said a minute ago... I know it sounds really far-fetched. But yes, they definitely feel connected to me. The mold and the bad wiring poisoning all my belongings... that's exactly why the neighbors are keeping an eye on us. They know what's happening, and they're just watching to see when I finally mess up again. It doesn't feel like separate things at all. It's all just... happening together.

When you first started hearing the water and voices seven months ago, were you already feeling heavy, tired, and depressed at that same time? Or did the depression and fatigue come later, after you started experiencing the voices and visions?

I was already feeling that way. The heavy, tired feeling came first. I mean, before the house problems dragged on and I really fell into this depression, I never heard voices in the walls. I didn't see wet patches that weren't there, or think the neighbors were tracking me. 

All of that... it only showed up after I had already stopped caring about my usual life. The voices and the visions only started after I was already just feeling like a failure every single day. So, yeah, the depression was definitely there first.
Before these past seven months, have you ever had another period lasting at least two weeks where you felt deeply depressed, hopeless, or lost interest in things you normally enjoyed?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days before, like anyone else. But... no, never anything like this. I've never had a time where I felt this hopeless or just completely lost interest in things for weeks on end. Before these past seven months, I was... I was doing fine. It really all just started with this current situation.
